A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 29-page versions of Symmetry-Aware GFlowNets. Their corresponding text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-graph, molecule-generation, likelihood-estimation, and runtime experiments, including additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Reward Scaling, Flow Scaling, fragment corrections, and the likelihood estimator retain their procedures and formulas. The new distribution-learning discussion explains their relationship to other formulations without introducing a new algorithm component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the illustrative and synthetic graph environments, atom- and fragment-based molecule tasks, molecular timing datasets, and appendix cycle-reward environment. Distribution learning is discussed but not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Synthetic comparisons retain Vanilla, Transition Correction, PE (Ma et al., 2024), and the same proposed correction variants. Molecule and timing experiments also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Appendix K.1 changes the illustrative experiment's probability of selecting actions uniformly from 0.1 to 0.9. This revises one reported experimental setting; the PDFs do not establish whether it corrects the description or reflects a rerun. Other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The feature-augmentation ablation in Appendix E.2, likelihood-estimation sensitivity analysis, runtime scalability analysis in Appendix J, and fragment-frequency analysis in Appendix L.2 are retained without additional tests or revised findings.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting remains unchanged, including mean and standard deviation over three timing runs in Table 5 and standard-deviation bands for likelihood-estimation errors in Figure 3(d). No run counts, seed information, or statistical procedures are added.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and plotted data match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains fragment Top K rewards of 0.941 ± 0.002 for Vanilla and 0.952 ± 0.003 for exact Reward Scaling. Appendix result tables and figures are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Corollary 5.1 and Theorem 5.2 now explicitly require node-by-node generation. Appendix I adds an explicit orbit-product count in its ordering discussion, and Appendix G corrects a flow-matching summation domain. The central correction results and proofs remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's contributions are unchanged. The conclusion now names Flow Scaling and repeats reward-structure dependence already discussed in v1, while retaining the same central claims about symmetry-bias correction and unbiased likelihood estimation.

C2.justification: Section 5 extends v1's ordering discussion to variational distribution learning, explicitly distinguishing correction requirements for backward-policy sampling and ordering-based sampling. Existing limitations concerning graph actions, GNN expressiveness, and molecule-task rewards remain.

D1.justification: Appendix K.1 revises the documented exploration hyperparameter from 0.1 to 0.9 for the illustrative experiment. Other implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained; moved metric and fragment-correction descriptions are not new disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix I expand the comparison with distribution-learning approaches, explicitly contrasting their ordering-based result with Chen et al. (2021) and discussing that work's orbit-count approximation. The bibliography is unchanged, although Appendix I introduces two unresolved '?' citations.

P1.justification: v2 adds a distribution-learning subsection, rewrites Appendix I, expands Appendix G's explanation, and makes limited theorem, conclusion, and wording edits. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Existing displays are reflowed: Figure 3 moves from PDF page 7 to 8, and Table 5 moves from page 25 to 24. Appendix I replaces displayed equations with inline expressions. No figures or tables are added, removed, or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision by making the node-by-node conditions explicit and explaining the distribution-learning connection more clearly. These gains improve exposition without changing the empirical evidence. Two unresolved citations detract from polish, and the unexplained exploration-setting revision cannot be credited as a validated experimental improvement.
